cases.name: Civic gateway between learning and hall
cases.concept: A low civic gateway stands between a three-storey learning bar and a community hall and forms the only enclosed passage between them. Everyone arrives through the gateway, where the school's front and its making and reading spaces meet visitors; classrooms extend behind it on one side and the shared hall on the other.
cases.intent: Aims to give staff a single supervised threshold controlling access to both classrooms and hall, and to let evening visitors reach the hall and arts without entering classroom corridors.

key_moves.move: School front and reading room in the gateway
key_moves.serves: Puts supervision, the nurse and the reading room at the threshold everyone passes through.
Makes the gateway the sole enclosed route between the learning bar and the hall.

key_moves.move: Arts and service on the hall side
key_moves.serves: Lets the hall, art and music, and kitchen receiving work as an after-hours cluster away from classrooms.
Keeps every classroom and special education room together behind the gateway.

core.statement: The civic gateway remains the only enclosed connection between the learning bar and the hall.
Administration, medical and media stay together in the gateway, with media above administration.
Art, music and custodial stay in the gateway beside the hall so the cluster can run with the learning bar closed.
All core academic and special education rooms stay in the single learning bar.

flexible: Whether kindergartens share the bar's ground floor with special education
Extent of the gateway's upper floor around the media center
Position of the health instructor's office within the hall
Sequence of rooms along the gateway's ground floor

brief_response.main_tradeoff: Keeping the gateway and hall low to hold the threshold at a human scale gives up three floors in every mass and leaves the gateway with a small upper floor.

unresolved: Gateway upper floor holds only the media center; uneven floor plates may conflict with uniform mass extrusion and GFA tolerance
Hall ground floor approaches the largest footprint the length and ratio limits allow
Gym and dining recorded on floor 1; their double-height volume rises through floor 2
Learning bar must hold the 80-ft depth while satisfying the footprint ratio

cases.name: Shared heart with two wings
cases.concept: A shared heart gathers the school's communal life: the hall for play, dining and assembly, crowned by a studio loft for art and music. Two wings, one of classrooms and one forming the school's front with its inclusive support, attach only to the heart, so all movement between them passes through it.
cases.intent: Seeks to make daily crossings through the heart a social routine that brings students from both wings together at lunch, assembly and arts, and to give the community one focal destination.

key_moves.serves: Routes every movement between the two wings through the shared heart.
Concentrates all communal and performing life in the heart, with arts linked to the stage below.
Pairs special education with the office and nurse, beneath a reading room above administration.

key_moves.move: Classroom wing over a service base
key_moves.serves: Keeps the classroom wing instructional, with custodial at its ground floor reaching the kitchen through the heart.

core.statement: The two wings connect only through the heart, never directly.
Art and music stay in the heart, in a loft above the hall.
Special education stays in the front wing with administration, medical and media.
The classroom wing holds core academic and custodial only.

flexible: Split of special education rooms between floors 1 and 2
Position of the stage relative to the studio loft
Location of custodial within the classroom wing's ground floor
Placement of the health instructor's office within the heart

brief_response.main_tradeoff: Lifting art and music into a loft above the heart gives up their ground-floor preference, and special education reaches core classrooms only by crossing the heart.

unresolved: Studio loft covers only part of the area over the hall; partial upper volume to check against uniform extrusion and GFA tolerance
Long-span structure carrying the loft over gym and dining unverified
Both wings contain academic or special education and must be 80-ft bars; their floor plates are uneven
Gym and dining recorded on floor 1; their double-height volume rises through floor 2

cases.name: Self-contained school bar, freestanding pavilions
cases.concept: One self-contained school bar carries the whole teaching day, rising from the front office and specialist support at its foot through classrooms to a reading crown. Two freestanding pavilions, a community hall and a making-and-maintenance workshop, stand apart on shared grounds and are reached outdoors.
cases.intent: Aims to let the hall and workshop open to the community and be phased independently, while keeping the instructional day secure inside a single enclosed bar.

key_moves.serves: Places supervision, support, classrooms and the reading crown in one enclosure, with media above administration.
Lets the hall stand alone for independent community use and phasing.
Groups art, music and custodial in a separate workshop pavilion on the grounds.

core.statement: Administration, medical, special education, core academic and media all stay in the one school bar.
The hall and workshop remain freestanding with no built links to the bar or each other.
Art, music and custodial share the workshop pavilion.

flexible: Which of art or music takes the workshop's upper floor
Arrangement of support rooms along the bar's ground floor
Distribution of classrooms between floors 2 and 3
Covered outdoor routes between the pavilions

brief_response.main_tradeoff: Detachment sends students outdoors for lunch, physical education and arts, separates custodial receiving from the kitchen, and the low pavilions forgo three floors.

unresolved: Outdoor walks to hall and workshop need weather protection, which is not modelled as a link
Bar ground floor carries administration, medical and special education together, near the capacity of an 80-ft bar
Custodial receiving sits apart from the kitchen and cannot be split; delivery arrangement unresolved
Gym and dining recorded on floor 1; their double-height volume rises through floor 2

cases.name: Courtyard ring with reading loft
cases.concept: Three ranges close around a courtyard and join at every corner into a continuous indoor loop: a tall learning range, a low civic and arts front, and a commons range whose hall is crowned by a reading loft that looks down into the court.
cases.intent: Seeks a protected outdoor room that every part of the school opens onto, with indoor circulation around it, and places reading at the social centre above shared dining.

key_moves.serves: Links every range to both others so circulation rings the courtyard.
Puts the library above the hall as the court's social centre.
Keeps the front range single-storey so the court stays open to light on that side.
Concentrates all classrooms and special education in the range that rises over the court.

core.statement: All three ranges stay directly linked into a closed loop around the courtyard.
The media center sits over the commons, not with administration.
The front stays single-storey, holding administration, medical, arts and custodial.
Core academic and special education stay together in the learning range.

flexible: Which corner of the loop serves as the main entrance

Position of the stage relative to the court

brief_response.main_tradeoff: Crowning the commons with the library gives up media above administration, and keeping the front single-storey beside a double-height commons forgoes three floors in every mass.

unresolved: Whether three masses can enclose a usable courtyard cannot be checked without site geometry
Reading loft covers only part of the area over the hall; partial upper volume to check against uniform extrusion and GFA tolerance
Single-storey front carries four departments on one floor; footprint to check against length and ratio limits

cases.name: Low classrooms beside civic tower
cases.concept: Classrooms stay low and close to the ground in a two-storey learning bar, flanked by the hall on one side and, on the other, a compact three-storey civic tower that stacks the school's front, its specialist support and a library crown as the building's vertical marker.
cases.intent: Aims to keep every classroom within one stair of the ground and close to the hall, while giving the school a clear civic address and grouping supervision, nursing and special education support.

key_moves.serves: Holds all core classrooms to the two lowest floors.
Gives the school its vertical marker, with media crowning administration and arts at grade.
Joins hall and tower only through the classroom bar, with custodial at the bar's hall end.

core.statement: Core academic never rises above floor 2.
Administration, medical, arts, special education and media stay stacked in the one civic tower.
The learning bar is the only mass linked to both the hall and the tower.

flexible: Split of classrooms between the bar's two floors

brief_response.main_tradeoff: Holding classrooms to two storeys forgoes three floors in every mass and lifts special education into the tower, away from both the ground and the core classrooms.

collection_differences: Concepts differ in what organizes movement: a civic gateway threshold (S01), a shared heart every wing passes through (S02), a self-contained school bar with freestanding pavilions (S03), a closed courtyard loop (S04), and low classrooms beside a civic tower (S05). Structurally, the middle of the chain differs (gateway in S01, heart in S02, learning bar in S05); S03 has no links and S04 links every pair. Art and music sit above the hall only in S02; media leaves administration only in S04. Special education shares the classroom mass in S01, S03 and S04, and joins the front in S02 and S05. Only S02 reaches three floors in every mass; the others keep the hall or front low.
